paper_metadata.title: Analysis of a hybrid quantum network for classification tasks

summary: This paper studies a hybrid quantum-classical neural network for classification on a 6-feature credit-scoring dataset and MNIST, using TensorFlow Quantum simulation with 8 qubits and 8 layers in the main finance experiments. On the balanced finance sample, the data-reuploading QNet reaches 0.78 train ACC / 0.86 train AUC and 0.68 test ACC / 0.72 test AUC, while on MNIST the QNet reaches 0.98 train ACC and 0.81 test ACC, matching the classical baseline on test accuracy. The paper also reports MNIST regularization results with dropout probability 0.58 yielding about 0.75 train/test ACC after 30 epochs.

experiments.description: Hybrid quantum-classical neural network (QNet) for binary credit-scoring classification on a balanced finance dataset, compared against a classical neural network baseline; includes a data re-uploading variant and a non-reuploading variant.

algorithm.variant: hybrid classical-quantum neural network with variational quantum classifier; compared with and without data re-uploading
algorithm.ansatz: per-qubit Ry-Rz-Ry rotations with CNOT entanglement; repeated for nlayers
algorithm.convergence_criteria: trained for 30 epochs (reported for regularization experiments; main finance results reported at nqubits = nlayers = 8)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: classical features are first compressed by a classical neural network into parameters fed to the quantum circuit; quantum part uses rotation angles on each qubit
problem_formulation.objective_function: binary classification of credit-scoring default vs non-default; minimize categorical crossentropy

problem_instance.description: Credit-scoring dataset classification, balanced sample I

dataset_specification.preprocessing: features scaled to [0,1]; sample I balanced to 50% default rate
dataset_specification.train_test_split: training data of 340 observations; separate test data used, size not reported

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: scaled features to [0,1]; balanced the default rate to 50% for sample I
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: reported ACC and AUC on training and test sets; compared QNet variants against classical NNet

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: classical neural network compresses input features before quantum circuit
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: classical output layer with softmax activation processes qubit measurements

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: training and test performance reported; no numeric loss curve values given

speedup_claims.conditions: balanced credit-scoring dataset; nqubits = nlayers = 8; compared on ACC and AUC
speedup_claims.caveats: No asymptotic speedup is shown; improvement is empirical and metric-dependent. Overfitting is observed.

speedup_claims.factor: data re-uploading superior to non-reuploading variant
speedup_claims.caveats: Comparison is within the quantum model family, not against a classical algorithm.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No practical advantage demonstrated; reported on 8 qubits and 8 layers in simulation only.
limiting_factors: classical baseline is competitive and sometimes better on test AUC
data loading/compression is classical, so end-to-end advantage is not established

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_other because the paper states all calculations were done with TensorFlow Quantum simulators and no physical QPU was used.
Circuit depth inferred from nlayers = 8 and the described repeated variational structure; the paper does not provide a transpiled depth or gate counts.
Speedup order set to none_proven because the paper reports empirical performance comparisons only and does not establish asymptotic quantum speedup.
Authors report the hybrid model outperforms a classical NNet on some metrics for the balanced finance dataset, but this is empirical and not a demonstrated quantum advantage.

experiments.description: Hybrid quantum-classical neural network (QNet) for multiclass MNIST digit classification, compared against a classical neural network baseline; main reported configuration uses 1000 training images and 10,000 test images.

algorithm.variant: hybrid classical-quantum neural network with variational quantum classifier; data re-uploading used in reported MNIST scalability plots
algorithm.ansatz: per-qubit Ry-Rz-Ry rotations with CNOT entanglement; repeated for nlayers
algorithm.convergence_criteria: trained for 30 epochs in regularization experiments; MNIST main results report training/test performance after training

hyperparameters.layer_sweep: multiple values of nlayers (exact values not fully enumerated in text)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: a classical neural network compresses 784 MNIST pixel features into parameters for the quantum circuit; multiclass softmax output used
problem_formulation.objective_function: 10-class handwritten digit classification; minimize categorical crossentropy

dataset_specification.preprocessing: grayscale 28x28 images; classical preprocessing compresses features before quantum circuit

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: grayscale images of size 28x28; classical neural network used to downscale features to the number of qubits
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: training and test ACC reported; confusion matrix shown; dependence on number of qubits and layers evaluated

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: classical neural network compresses 784 input features before quantum circuit
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: classical output layer with softmax activation processes qubit measurements

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: learning progress compared between QNet and NNet; no numeric loss curve values given

speedup_claims.conditions: MNIST with 1000 training images and 10,000 test images; compared during training and on test data
speedup_claims.caveats: No runtime numbers are reported; claim is based on learning curves and accuracy only.

speedup_claims.factor: slightly better training accuracy than classical baseline
speedup_claims.caveats: Test accuracy is the same; overfitting is present in both models.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No practical advantage demonstrated; 1000 training images and 10,000 test images on a simulator with 2-12 qubits.
limiting_factors: test ACC is 0.81 for both QNet and NNet
training ACC is higher for QNet (0.98 vs 0.83), but generalization is not better
classical feature compression is essential, so quantum part is not end-to-end responsible for performance

notes: The paper reports MNIST results for varying qubit counts (2, 4, 8, 12) and varying layers, but does not specify a single fixed qubit count for the main MNIST experiment; therefore num_qubits is left null and marked inferred from the sweep context.
Circuit depth is not explicitly stated for the main MNIST experiment; only layer sweeps are discussed, so depth is left null and marked inferred/unspecified.
Hardware inferred as simulator_other because the paper states all calculations were done with TensorFlow Quantum simulators and no physical QPU was used.
Speedup order set to none_proven because the paper reports empirical performance comparisons only and does not establish asymptotic quantum speedup.
The paper reports faster training convergence for QNet, but test performance is equal to the classical baseline at 0.81 ACC.

experiments.description: Regularization experiment for the MNIST hybrid quantum-classical network using dropout between the quantum and second classical network.

algorithm.variant: hybrid classical-quantum neural network with dropout regularization
algorithm.ansatz: same QNet architecture as MNIST experiment; dropout applied to measurement values

key_results: With dropout probability 0.58, training ACC ≈ test ACC ≈ 0.75 after 30 epochs.
This is reported in Section 6, 'The simplest method is to add a dropout layer... Fixing this parameter to 0.58 we achieve our result to get training ACC ≈ test ACC ≈ 0.75 after 30 epochs.'

experiments.description: Regularization experiment for the MNIST hybrid quantum-classical network using L2 regularization on measurement values.

algorithm.variant: hybrid classical-quantum neural network with L2 regularization on measurement values
algorithm.ansatz: same QNet architecture as MNIST experiment; L2 penalty applied to measurement values

key_results: Regularizing measurement results reduces overfitting and improves agreement between training and validation ACC.
The paper states that regularizing the angles fed into the quantum net destroys classification performance, while regularizing measurement results can be fine-tuned to avoid overfitting.
